meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: + dative: верить мне. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to believe', paired with 'поверить'.
Верить в + accusative. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to believe', paired with 'поверить'.

examples.trans: Go on, tell her. Nina doesn't believe it.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Drawing attention. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.
Drawing attention. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.trans: I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: For emphasis.

examples.trans: I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я знаю всё в моём отеле.
examples.trans: I know everything in my hotel.

meanings.note: 'закрывать глаза на' + accusative = to turn a blind eye to

examples.text: Я не буду закрывать на это глаза.
examples.trans: I'm not going to close my eyes to this.

examples.text: А я глаза на это закрывать не буду. Я подниму людей!
examples.trans: Well, I'm not going to close my eyes to this. I'll rally people!

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Disbelief. Core Russian part meaning 'yes' in everyday speech.
'два' with masculine/neuter nouns, 'две' with feminine; the noun goes into the genitive singular

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

meanings.note: Singular only. Common feminine noun meaning 'food, meal' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: В этом ресторане всегда свежая еда.
examples.trans: There is always fresh food in this restaurant.
Oh no, bad food? Does your stomach hurt?

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see
Core Russian adv meaning 'more; still; yet' in everyday speech.
Ещё больше = even more. Core Russian adv meaning 'more; still; yet' in everyday speech.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: + accusative. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to wait, to expect', paired with 'подождать'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to wait, to expect', paired with 'подождать'.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'бежать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'I will drop by'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и забежать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and I will drop by on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют забежать.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to I will drop by.

related.gloss: not to I will drop by (negated infinitive)

meanings.note: В интернете = on the internet. International borrowing from English 'Internet' ('inter-' + 'network').

examples.trans: Look it up on the internet.
Look it up on the internet.

meanings.note: In questions. Core Russian det meaning 'what; what a' in everyday speech.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Agreeing, often reluctantly. Core Russian part meaning 'all right, OK' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: пойти в магазин = to go to the shop

examples.trans: What to do? Let's go to the shop.

meanings.note: Short for может быть. Core Russian part meaning 'maybe, perhaps' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I thought maybe you wouldn't see me.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Надо + infinitive. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'писать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to write', paired with 'писать'.

examples.text: А зачем? Я сам сделал так, чтобы он его написал.
examples.trans: And why would I? I'm the one who made him write it.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Colloquial. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('normal').
Colloquial. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('normal').
short form 'нужен / нужна / нужно / нужны' + dative: 'мне нужна работа' = I need a job
Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'promotion' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Или просто попроси у шефа повышения.
examples.trans: Or simply ask the chef for a promotion.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть повышение.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always promotion.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('raise').

examples.text: Макс, надо у Германа просить повышение зарплаты!
examples.trans: Max, we need to ask German for a salary raise!

examples.text: Парни, да бросьте вы, какое сейчас повышение?
examples.trans: Guys, come on, what raise right now?

meanings.note: + dative. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мочь'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to help', paired with 'помогать'.

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'help' in everyday Russian.
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'просить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to ask (for), to request', paired with 'просить'.

examples.trans: I wanted to ask you something.
Arkash, I wanted to ask you something.

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look
meanings.note: One completed look. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a look', paired with 'смотреть'.
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a look', paired with 'смотреть'.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine

meanings.note: takes the accusative; everyday synonym of о

examples.text: Как интересно! А в Москве ты про меня гадости рассказываешь.
examples.trans: How interesting! And in Moscow you go around saying nasty things about me.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'max', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Я уже вылила это вино в раковину, Макс!
examples.trans: I already poured that wine down the sink, Max!
Do you mind that this is our sink?

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('connected / tied').

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень связанный выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very connected choice.

examples.text: У нас сегодня просто связанный день в ресторане.
examples.trans: We are having a simply connected day at the restaurant today.

meanings.note: The г sounds like в.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

Polite request. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: там такие деньги = there's so much money in it

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
